LEARN (in the Detection panel header) listens to your track for about 8 seconds and suggests Sensitivity, Gap Threshold and Min Gap that suit it. Play representative, rhythmic material through GapFill while it listens. You always see the suggestion first: Apply sets the three values (one Undo step), Discard changes nothing, and Revert restores the old values.

It needs real playback (not an offline render) and a signal above -60 dBFS for a quarter of the time. Pads and other material without clear hits are reported as such and left alone. DETERMINISTIC CO-OP adds reproducible ownership alongside the original Avoid overlap, Alternate and Follow modes. The original mode and group controls keep their old ranges and automation. Choose a deterministic group, or Use legacy group, then give every track a unique fixed slot. New duplicate slots are assigned a free slot; the assigned number is saved with the project.

Priority controls relative ownership share. Yield reduces non-owner Density and Fill; at 100 only the owner may start natural fills. It never makes an unsafe gap eligible. A lone instance is unchanged. The lowest fixed slot chooses the shared grid; all tracks use the same version of membership at a future musical boundary. Changes may wait while another live track has not advanced. Without valid host transport cooperation pauses and ordinary timing remains available.

GROUP RECALL schedules the selected scene index from each member's own bank at one common future PPQ boundary. Bank contents are not copied between tracks. A missing scene, late delivery, lost transport or seek cancels that receiver's request with a status message; it never applies late. Group cancellation, membership changes and participant teardown cancel outstanding requests. Panic keeps its existing dry-safe behavior and cancels pending group recalls.

Cooperation works only between instances of the same loaded plugin format in one process. It uses no network, files or OS IPC. Sandboxed or bridged tracks may see only themselves; the status explains this. The registry supports 32 live instances. Original live modes retain their timing-dependent behavior. Save unique fixed slots before comparing offline and real-time renders.

Evolve slowly changes the character of the fills on its own, so a long section keeps moving. Every 8, 16 or 32 bars it glides towards the centre of one of the Surprise Me styles (for example Tape Breakdown or Glitch Storm), in an order that depends on the Seed and never repeats the same style twice in a row.

Evolve needs a playing transport and a known time signature; without them it does nothing. The current style is shown next to the Evolve control.

Most effects process everything they are given. GapFill does the opposite: it listens for the musical events in your audio, works out where the usable spaces between those events are, and puts generated ear candy only in those spaces - while actively protecting the original hits.
The material for those fills is cut from your own recent audio, so what appears in the gaps still sounds like your track rather than a canned sample.
Rule one inside GapFill is simple: the original hit is more important than the fill.
1.  Insert GapFill on a drum loop, drum bus or percussion track and press play.
2.  Watch the visualiser. White lines are detected events, the blue tint is space GapFill considers usable, the amber strip is protection, the bar underneath shows fills.
3.  Turn FILL up from 0%. Around 25-35% you get occasional ear candy between hits.
4.  Raise INTENSITY and COMPLEXITY for bigger, more elaborate fills.
5.  If the original hits start to lose definition, raise TRANSIENT PROTECT.
6.  If the kick or sub gets cluttered, set LOW PROTECT to around 100 Hz.
7.  Nothing happening? Raise SENSITIVITY, raise GAP THRESHOLD, or lower MINIMUM GAP.

TRANSIENT follows attacks and works best on drums, percussion, plucks and rhythmic bass. PHRASE uses slower envelopes plus spectral change, so it reacts to phrase endings instead of every consonant - use it for vocals, melodies, guitars and pads. SPECTRAL analyses low, mid and high separately, so a busy kick does not stop GapFill using the empty top end.

MAIN listens to the track GapFill is on. SIDECHAIN uses the sidechain input purely for timing - the fills are still built from this track's audio. HYBRID takes the spaces from the sidechain but still protects important events on this track.
how easily an event is detected. Too low and quiet hits are missed; too high and GapFill triggers on noise and tails.
how far energy must fall, relative to the local musical reference level, before a region counts as space. Higher values accept less silence as a gap. Digital silence is never required.
spaces shorter than this never get a fill. This is the main control for keeping GapFill out of busy passages.
the longest a single fill may last. Can be tempo-synced with SYNC MAX FILL.

how long GapFill waits before deciding an event has really ended. Short values react instantly; long values only accept settled pauses. Note that the opposite direction is always instant - a new hit collapses the gap immediately.
a safe region straight after each detected hit where no fill may start, so the body of the hit is never covered.
minimum time between two detected events, so one hit is not counted several times.

lets GapFill see what is coming, so fills can be faded out before the next important event. This is reported to the host as plugin latency and the dry path is delayed to match. Set to 0 ms for zero-latency work.
monitor exactly what the detector hears - the main track, or the sidechain when sidechain detection is active. Very useful for setting Sensitivity.

the primary amount. It is a probability, not a wet/dry control: 0% generates nothing, 10-25% gives occasional subtle candy, 25-50% is clearly audible while the groove survives, 50-75% is active transformation and 75-100% fills nearly every usable space.
how hard each fill is processed - pitch range, drive, crushing, filter resonance, stereo movement. It is deliberately not a level control.

how elaborate a fill may become. Low means a single simple transformation. High stacks up to three carefully chosen extra transformations and unlocks the granular and spectral algorithms. It does not make anything louder.
variation and unpredictability: algorithm choice, timing, pitch, grain behaviour and stereo movement. Even at 100% everything stays bounded.
how many of the eligible spaces actually get used. Separate from Wet, so you can have loud but rare fills, or quiet but constant ones.

AUTO weighs every enabled algorithm against the length of the gap, how hard the hit that opened it was, the macros and which algorithms were used recently. It will not choose something that cannot fit, and it avoids repeating itself unless Chaos is low.
plays a recent fragment backwards, typically swelling into the next hit.
repeats a short slice on a musical subdivision, optionally accelerating, decelerating or stepping in pitch.
a short echo pattern built from the material right before the gap, with optional ping-pong. It always ends inside the gap.
a cloud of short grains taken from the last second or so of audio, with pitch, position, pan and reverse variation.
captures a short region and sustains it with a proper crossfaded loop.
a fragment whose pitch glides up or down across the gap.
animates a low-pass, high-pass or band-pass sweep across a captured slice.
synthesises a short noise texture shaped by the track's own band energies, so it belongs to the material rather than sounding pasted on.
controlled digital degradation - bit reduction plus sample-rate decimation.
saturation and foldback applied to the fill only. The protected original hit stays clean.
rearranges small slices of the captured material, keeping the timing musical rather than purely random.
an FFT smear that removes transients and leaves ghostly transitional material. Only one spectral fill runs at a time to bound CPU use.
a short tuned resonance excited by the captured audio. It decays inside the gap instead of ringing forever.
replays the hit that opened the gap while the virtual tape deck brakes to a halt, losing speed, pitch and top end. Intensity sets how hard it brakes; Chaos adds a little wow.

(Creative panel) freezes the fill source. While it is on, every fill is built from the audio heard at the moment you pressed it, even as the track moves on - detection, protection and the dry signal keep following the live input. Turn it off to release. It needs half a second of audio before it can latch, and it is automatable and MIDI-learnable for live performance.

Each algorithm has a weight from 0 to 100%. Zero disables it completely. The weights only matter when Fill Type is AUTO. The RHYTHMIC and TEXTURAL buttons are quick starting points: rhythmic favours reverses, stutters, delays and crushing, textural favours granular, freeze, spectral and comb.
This is what separates GapFill from a random glitch effect. All of it acts on the generated material only - the dry signal is never touched.
ducks generated material around strong detected attacks so the original hits keep their impact.
high-passes the fills. Around 80-150 Hz keeps kick and sub clean while everything above still gets treated. Fully left is Off.
pushes fills progressively out to the sides, protecting centred kick, snare, bass and lead vocal. At high settings the wet material is almost entirely on the sides.
uses lookahead to fade or duck the fill as the next important event approaches, and at high settings fades it to silence exactly on the hit.
when sidechain detection is active, strong sidechain hits force generated material out of the way. Think event-aware masking rather than a static sidechain compressor.

In SPECTRAL detector mode the signal is split with proper Linkwitz-Riley crossovers into LOW, MID and HIGH, and each lane finds its own spaces. A kick can keep the low lane busy while the high lane is wide open, and GapFill will place a high-frequency fill there without touching the kick's energy.

Each lane has its own enable, fill amount, intensity and probability. Generated material is band-limited to the lane it was scheduled in. Use SOLO / AUDITION to listen to one lane on its own and hear exactly what that detector sees.

Route another track into GapFill's sidechain input in your DAW, then set Detector Source to SIDECHAIN or HYBRID. The sidechain decides WHEN there is space; the track GapFill is on still provides WHAT the fills are made of.
GapFill on bass, drums to sidechain
manipulated bass fragments appear between the drum hits.
GapFill on vocals, drums to sidechain
vocal echoes, grains and reverses land rhythmically around the drums.
GapFill on a synth, kick to sidechain
generated synth material stays out of the kick.
If the sidechain is selected but nothing is connected (or it has been silent for several seconds), GapFill falls back to main detection and the status line tells you so. Audio is never interrupted.

GapFill's randomness is deterministic. With a running transport the decision for a gap is derived from the seed and the musical position, so the same bar plays back the same way every time and a reopened project sounds identical.

generates a genuinely new creative setup on every press - new macros, new algorithm weights and a new seed that is guaranteed to differ from the previous one. Detector settings and mix levels are left alone.
also randomises detection and protection within safe musical ranges.

jumps to one of eight curated creative profiles - Subtle Sparkle, Drum Edits, Glitch Storm, Dub Echoes, Ambient Haze, Pitch Bender, Industrial Grit or Tape Breakdown - with fresh variation each time and never the same profile twice in a row. Unlike RANDOM, the result is always coherent; detector, protection and mix are untouched.
steps back through the last 32 whole-sound changes: RANDOM, RANDOM ALL, SURPRISE, RESET, preset changes and file loads.
returns every parameter to its default value.
Randomising never touches Dry, Wet, Output, Lookahead or Bypass, so it cannot produce a dangerous level or an unexpected latency change.
independent levels for the original and the generated material.

the button under the readouts. WET ONLY sends only what GapFill generates to the main output, at unity, with no dry signal: Dry and Wet are shown dimmed and ignored, Output still applies, bypass wins. A WET ONLY chip also appears in the footer next to PANIC so the state cannot be forgotten. Presets, Reset, Undo and file loads never change it.
stereo width of the fills only. Mono Wet collapses them for maximum mono compatibility.
input, fill and output levels, plus the live gap-confidence bar.

These are preferences, not parameters: they are never automated and never part of a preset.

ARRANGEMENT listens to how the music changes (loudness, how busy it is, which frequencies dominate) and finds the sections of the song. It starts in a Learning state where it does nothing. Calm thins out fills in quiet sections such as breakdowns, Lift makes fills more likely and longer just before an expected change and during a build, Settle holds fills back right after a section starts so the downbeat lands cleanly.

It never forces a fill into a protected or ineligible gap and never touches the dry sound. The result depends on what has played, so it relearns after a seek or loop restart. A single drum bus shows little structure; then it stays neutral.

The current arrangement model forecasts a change only after observing repeated periods. Irregular or unseen structures and invalid transport keep the forecast unknown. When transport is valid, estimates align to host bars and phrases; they remain estimates of the music, not promises. Existing projects retain their legacy arrangement model until you explicitly upgrade it.
Alternates two stored fill styles, A and B, every 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars. Needs host transport and a time signature. Host automation and your own settings are never changed: the styles are applied on top.
Store the current sound (creative, weights, effects and musical settings) as style A.
Store the current sound (creative, weights, effects and musical settings) as style B.
Take styles from the header A and B
Use the header A snapshot as style A and the header B snapshot as style B. Copy a sound into B first (COPY), change it, then press this.
Forget both stored styles. The Beat Battle switch stays where it is but does nothing until two styles are stored.

Beat Battle alternates two fill styles, A and B, in time with the music. Set up a sound you like and press STORE A, change it, press STORE B (or press FROM A/B to take the header A and B snapshots), then choose how often to switch: every 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars. Even windows play A, odd windows play B, counted from the start of the song, so looping and seeking give the same pattern.

It needs host transport and a time signature, and two different styles; the line under the controls says what is missing. A style holds the creative, weight, effect and musical settings. Your own settings and host automation are never changed: the styles are applied on top while a battle runs. The styles are not saved with the project.
GapFill listens to its last few fills and answers with a complementary (or similar) character. It only nudges choices.
How strongly the response is steered.
How many fills to listen to before answering.

Call and response watches GapFill's own last few fills (the call), summarises them as a motif, and shapes the next few fills (the response). Complement answers with a different kind of fill, Echo with a similar one. It only nudges the odds and lengths: it never creates or removes fills, and it never changes what counts as a gap.

A forced Fill Type, Fill Lock and More Like That take precedence and pause it. Response fills are marked "Response" in History, so you can lock one. When the last fills do not form a clear motif, the chip says "No response" and fills stay ordinary.
Freeze the source: fills keep using the audio heard when Capture was switched on, while detection, protection and the dry signal follow the live input. Switch off to release.
Installs the note and CC bindings of a known controller (replaces the command bindings).
MIDI output that mirrors Panic, hold and scene state on the controller's lights. Standalone only.

Where the swell peaks: the end of the gap, the next beat or the next bar.

Effects are optional extras that shape the generated fill material. Each one is off at Amount 0 and sounds exactly like GapFill without it. The Effects section lists them in the order the audio passes through them: Reverse Swell and Granular Cloud (modes of two fill types), then Ratchet, Tape Destruction and Rhythmic Crush. Controls appear once an effect is switched on. Effects only ever process the generated wet signal; your dry signal and the protection of hits are untouched.
The switch next to a name sets Amount to 0 and remembers it. Solo sets Fill Type to the algorithm an effect is a mode of.

Reverse Swell is a mode of the Reverse fill type: the sound just before the hit that opened the gap is played backwards so it rises and brightens into a landing point, then stops short of the next hit. Amount is the chance that a Reverse fill becomes a swell. Raise the Reverse weight, or press Solo, to hear it more often.
Linear, Exponential, S-curve or Late: how the level builds.
How far a low-pass opens during the swell. 0 keeps the colour constant.
Gap end, the next beat or the next bar. Beat and bar need the host transport; without it the swell lands at the end of the gap and the card says so.

Granular Cloud is a mode of the Granular fill type with direct control of the grains. Amount is the chance that a Granular fill becomes a cloud. The cloud is limited to 48 grains at once and the card shows when the density was lowered to stay inside that.
Grains per second and grain length.
How far back in time grains are taken from. While Capture is on, the captured sound is used.
0 takes every grain from the middle of the span; 100 spreads them evenly over it.
Random pitch (in cents, either way) and stereo position of each grain.

Ratchet re-triggers the start of a fill several times, speeding up or slowing down. Amount is the chance that a fill is ratcheted. The repeats follow the host tempo; without a transport a 120 BPM fallback is used and the card says so. Repeats never run past the end of the fill, so the next hit stays protected.
Number of repeats, including the first.
Positive makes each repeat shorter, negative longer. The shortest repeat is 8 ms.
How much of each repeat sounds.

Tape Destruction adds wow, flutter, saturation, dropouts and splices to a fill. It works with any fill type (Tape Stop is a separate fill type). Amount scales every control and blends the effect with the dry fill. The random events are seeded from the fill, so a fill with a given Seed repeats exactly.

Rhythmic Crush reduces bit depth and sample rate of the fill and can hold the sample for a musical division, stepping through a fixed 8-step pattern. Aliasing is part of the sound. This is separate from the Bit Crush fill type and the Crush modifier. Amount blends the crushed sound with the dry fill.
Free uses the Rate control; a division holds each sample for that length (at most 4096 samples).
Negative values darken, positive values remove low end.

In Spectral detection each fill belongs to a LOW, MID or HIGH lane. The LOW / MID / HIGH switches under the effects choose which lanes use them. A lane that is switched off stays free of effects; fills that cover the whole spectrum always use them.

Moves the resonant character of the sound (its formants) without changing its pitch. Amount blends the processed sound with the original. The effect works on the whole wet sound and delays it by about 21 ms (about 23 ms at 96 kHz); the next protected hit is still kept clear.
Up to 12 semitones either way. With Scale Lock on it snaps to an in-scale interval.
Brightens or darkens by up to 6 dB per octave around 1 kHz.
Adds vowel-like resonances. This colours the sound; it does not make words.
Rings the wet sound at a chosen pitch, like a tuned pipe. Amount is how much resonance is added to the sound.
Scale degrees picks an in-scale note near Note for every fill when Scale Lock is on; otherwise it behaves like Manual.
From 50 ms to 2 seconds of ringing.
An echo in which every repeat is shifted by a fixed number of Hz, so the repeats climb or sink. A shift of 0 is a plain damped echo. Tails stop after 4 seconds.
A feedback echo that darkens with every repeat and whose high cut moves over two bars. The feedback is limited to 90 % and a saturator keeps the loop level bounded, so it cannot run away.

Builds a reverb from one of your own hits: Capture IR takes the strongest hit of the last 4 seconds. The impulse is never saved with the project - after reopening, capture again (or load a WAV). Without an impulse the card passes the sound unchanged.

Freezes the sound just before a gap into a sustained texture. Auto capture does this at every fill; Capture freezes what is playing now and Release fades it out. A second capture lets Morph blend between two frozen sounds. The frozen sound starts about 43 ms after the capture.
Let the density and intensity of fills follow how busy the music is. Sparse passages get more fills; busy passages fewer but bolder. 0 = off.
Which setting the energy follow steers: Density, Intensity or Both.

Energy follow listens to how busy the music is compared with the last minute (loudness and how many hits per second) and shows it as Low, Mid or High. With Follow above 0, sparse passages get a higher fill density and softer fills, busy passages a lower density and bolder fills. Follows chooses whether density, intensity or both are steered.

It adapts to what has played: it needs about ten seconds to learn the range after you switch it on, changes class slowly on purpose, and relearns after Follow is set to 0. It is an estimate; a loud but sparse passage can read as busy.
Make the repeats of tempo-synced Stutter and Delay fills follow the swing of your music. Needs host tempo and Sync on. 0 = off.
The note grid the swing is measured against: 1/8 or 1/16.
Freeze the learned groove so it no longer changes.
Clear the groove and measure the next 8 bars. The groove is applied when the measurement ends, then held.
Forget the learned groove and start measuring again.

Groove listens to where your music's hits fall against the host's beat grid and makes the repeats of Stutter fills and the taps of Delay fills follow that feel, so a straight stutter over a swung hi-hat swings too. Only the wet repeats move; the start of a fill, the dry sound and the host timing never change.

It needs rhythmic input, host tempo and the Sync switch on. Below 35 % confidence it applies nothing and says the groove is unclear. LEARN measures 8 bars and then holds the result; HOLD freezes whatever has been learned so far; RESET forgets it.
How often a Granular fill rebuilds itself as stacked harmonies of the pitch heard in the source. 0 = off.
How many harmony layers play: unison, octave, fifth, third, octave down, two octaves up.
How much the grains drift through the source and detune.

Harmonic turns Granular fills into stacked harmonies of the note heard in the source. GapFill finds the pitch of the last moments before the fill; when the source is clearly pitched the grains are cut a whole number of periods long and replayed at musical intervals. With drums or noise it falls back to ordinary Granular and the strip says so.
Voices adds layers in this order: unison, octave, fifth, third, octave down, two octaves up. With Scale Lock on, the third is minor when the scale has one.
Hold a repeating stutter of the last moment of sound while pressed (Latch mode: toggles).
Hold a frozen wash of the last moment of sound.
Play the last moment of sound backwards while pressed.
Slow the last moment of sound to a stop.
Stutter Storm: a rapid accented stutter pattern on the 1/32 grid while pressed.
Starts a fill at the next beat or bar even without a gap (Options set when).
Spins the Glitch Roulette: a random, safe change to the fill settings.
Momentary holds only while pressed; Latch toggles on each press.
Lowers the dry signal while a hold is active.
Holds do not cover protected hits.
A latched hold releases after this many seconds.

The pads do what a MIDI note bound to the same command does. Stutter, Freeze, Reverse and Tape stop are hold effects: they play while the pad is held (Momentary) or toggle on each press (Latch). Storm is a short accented stutter burst. Fill Now starts a fill on the next beat or bar; Roulette makes a random, safe change to the settings.
Level sets the hold loudness, Dry duck lowers the dry signal while a hold plays, PROTECT keeps holds off protected hits, and Timeout releases a latched hold by itself. Panic releases every hold.
Listen to the music and use its key for Scale Lock instead of the Key and Scale you set by hand. Drums and noise give no key; then your manual setting is used.
Freeze the detected key and save it with the project, so renders are reproducible.
How many seconds of music the key is estimated from. Longer is steadier, shorter follows key changes sooner.
How sure the detector must be before Scale Lock follows the detected key. Below this your manual key is used.

AUTO KEY listens to the incoming music and estimates its key, for example A minor, with a confidence. While it is confident, Scale Lock uses that key instead of the Key and Scale you chose by hand. WET ONLY (also the OUTPUT button in the Mix panel, with a footer chip) makes the main output carry only what GapFill generates, at unity: Dry and Wet are ignored, Output still applies, bypass wins and Panic still silences it. It is a routing switch, so presets, Reset, Undo, opening a preset file, Random and scenes never change it (only your DAW project restores it). The optional Wet output bus (VST3 and CLAP, off until your DAW enables it) carries the same signal on its own output, aligned with the main output; Dry, Wet and Output do not touch it and bypass silences it.

SIDECHAIN GATE fills only while the sidechain is quiet (ducking) or only while it is active, using the threshold. SC SNAP moves a fill start to the nearest sidechain hit within 30 ms at 100 percent, never earlier than the gap start. Both do nothing until a sidechain input is connected.

MIDI OUT sends a note for every detected gap and a note one higher for every fill. It needs a build with MIDI output enabled, and some hosts ignore MIDI from effect plug-ins. Time-stamps are aligned with the delayed audio.

CO-OP lets GapFill instances in the same host process share a group (A to D). Avoid overlap and Follow react to what the other instances are doing right now, so their results can differ from run to run; Alternate gives each member every n-th bar and is repeatable. Hosts that run every plug-in in its own process cannot see each other: the status then reads no other GapFill found and nothing changes. Off shares nothing.

QUALITY trades richness for CPU. Balanced and Lite use fewer voices, grains and a shorter bus-effect tail; Lite also turns the formant, spectral freeze and convolution effects off. Latency never changes. Auto steps down when GapFill's own estimated load stays high and back up after a long calm period; it behaves as Full when the host renders offline. SCRUB freezes a snapshot of the last second of sound (while Capture is on, the captured sound) and loops a short window of it with smooth loop points. It lives in the Effects section (Creative tab, EFFECTS drawer): Position and Width appear once SCRUB is on. Position moves the window through the snapshot: it glides rather than jumping, and its speed is limited so scanning stays clean. Position can be automated or driven from a controller.

Switching SCRUB off fades out over about 8 ms. Panic (and a transport stop) also fades it out; switch SCRUB off and on again to restart it. The scrub sound follows the same protection of hits as fills.

TENSION moves density, intensity, width and effect amount along a curve that lasts a number of bars, then repeats, holds or releases. Each lane has a depth; 0 leaves that lane alone. Shapes: Build rises to the end, Build+Drop rises and then snaps back to neutral for the last eighth, Breakdown falls and returns, Swell rises and falls, Custom uses the curves you draw.

EDIT CURVES... opens the curve editor: pick a lane (Density, Intensity, Width, FX Send), drag a point to move it, double-click to add one (up to 16 per lane), right-click or Delete to remove it, and use BUILD, BUILD+DROP, BREAKDOWN or SWELL to start from a built-in shape. From the keyboard: Page Up and Page Down select a point, the arrow keys move it (Shift for ten times the step), Insert adds, Delete removes. The first edit switches Shape to Custom so you hear what you draw; the cyan line is the playhead.

The position comes from the host's bar count, so loops, seeks and offline renders land on the same value. Start bar counts from the start of the song and assumes a constant time signature. Without host tempo and time signature it does nothing. Curves are saved in the project, not in .gapfill parameter files.
